pageCache.text:
Discover Somerhill, Kent’s leading prep school for girls and boys aged 2–13. Renowned for exceptional preparation for top grammar and independent schools, the school offers unrivalled facilities set within 150 acres of beautiful parkland.
Academically ambitious yet non-selective, Somerhill consistently sends more pupils to grammar schools than any other school in the area. As a flagship PSB school, its skills-based curriculum nurtures curiosity, self-awareness and personal growth, preparing children confidently for the next stage of their education.
Beyond the classroom, pupils benefit from a rich co-curricular programme, including over 100 clubs, 480 music lessons each week and more than 600 sports fixtures annually. World-class facilities support this breadth of opportunity, from art and music studios to engineering and science labs, a dedicated Forest School, and extensive, unparalleled sports provision—all set within a unique historic parkland campus.
Many children begin their journey in Somerhill’s popular Pre-Prep, a warm and nurturing environment with specialist teachers and small class sizes tailored to each age group. Combined with the Saplings Forest School programme, it offers a carefully balanced approach to indoor and outdoor learning from age 2 upwards. Additionally, Somerhill has an extensive after-school care provision, including Breakfast Club and wraparound care.
With expert teaching from the earliest years, small classes and outstanding facilities, Somerhill provides a holistic education that fosters academic success, independence and confident, happy, well-rounded children.
Over 7000 books in our 400-year-old Woodgate Library
Over 100 extra-curricular clubs and activities each week
24 scholarship places gained in 2026
More grammar school places than any other local school
Over 600 sporting fixtures each year
More than 280 individual music lessons each week
"Pupils demonstrate excellent all-round achievement both academically and through their success in a wide range of co-curricular activity. They strive to do their best knowing they are supported and encouraged to have high expectations in this caring and happy school community."
ISI Inspection Report
“The perfect educational model…with stonking facilities…the green spaces will make you swoon.”
“We love being a part of this community. The teaching is excellent and my children have been so happy here with so many opportunities for learning, both inside the classroom and outside in the beautiful spacious grounds. Highly recommend whether your child is sporty, creative or academic!”
“What a great school with amazing facilities, after-school clubs and hands-on caring staff who bring out the best in each child. Our grandson cannot wait to get there each morning and his comment at the end of the day when asked what kind of day he’s had is “I’ve had a great day!” I think that says it all.”
Somerhill Grandparent
Pre-school at Somerhill
Children can join our pre-school from the age of 2. Our Saplings provision extends across Nursery and Kindergarten, offering a bespoke outdoor education to start their learning journey.
Pre-prep at Somerhill
Children can join our pre-prep from Reception until the end of Year 2. With a dedicated space, children flourish and grow as they continue their Somerhill journey.
Prep at Somerhill
Children join prep at age 7 and stay until age 11 for girls and 13 for boys. Classroom learning is single-sex but in our stunning co-educational environment.
Latest news
Follow us: @somerhillkent
Visit us today and discover Somerhill
We know that choosing the right school for your child is a big decision. At Somerhill, we take a personal and dedicated approach to help you at this important time. Whether you would like an informal chat, a visit or a meeting, our Admissions Team are on hand to make the arrangements or answer any questions, big or small.
Our three most common entry points at Somerhill are Nursery, Reception, and Year 3. Subject to availability, children can join us anytime during the school year. Our youngest pupils can join us for our Nursery provision when they are two years old. Children may also join in September, following their third birthday, when they can join our Kindergarten for the school year before Reception. Children are also welcome to join Somerhill directly at Reception.

Somerhill Prospectus
SOMERHILL We grow amazing people
A beautifully unique independent prep school for girls and boys aged 2-13
Welcome to Somerhill
We are delighted that you are interested in Somerhill for your child(ren). We have a very special school here with a unique offering: the ‘best of both worlds’, the ‘ideal mix’ and the ‘place I always dreamt of finding’ are the comments we often hear from our parents or visitors. With co-educational learning from 2-7 years, Somerhill then offers single-sex classroom lessons until children leave us for senior schools, allowing uninhibited learning and bespoke strategies for the older girls and boys with all the benefits of a co-educational setting. Our philosophy for the children at Somerhill is straightforward: happy children want to learn.
Children are happy if they can play, participate widely and start to master skills of whatever kind, and our stunning setting and outstanding facilities offer endless opportunities for children to find something that makes them smile. We believe this brochure offers you the perfect glimpse into our school life. However, to fully appreciate the extraordinary education that we offer and see our vision of confident, curious, and resilient children realised, we invite you to visit us at Somerhill. You will see that this is a beautifully unique school providing an exceptional learning environment where we grow amazing people!
The Good Schools Guide
Once a family home, now a family school
Housed in a 400-year-old Jacobean mansion, surrounded by 150 acres of glorious parkland, Somerhill is one of the most beautiful school settings you will find. From our picturesque lake to our woodland treehouse, our stunning surroundings enrich the children’s educational experience.
Every inch of our diverse and expansive site is exploited during break times, activities, and lessons as we blend indoor and outdoor learning throughout the school day.
“ What a great school with amazing facilities, after-school clubs and hands-on caring staff who bring out the best in each child. Our grandson cannot wait to get there each morning, and his comment at the end of the day when asked what kind of day he has had is ‘I’ve had a great day!’ I think that says it all.” Grandparent “ First-class teaching, wonderful staff, outstanding facilities… Somerhill has it all… and the outdoor spaces will take your breath away.” Parent
One way of living but two ways of learning
Between the ages of 2 and 7, girls and boys are together in the classroom. This environment promotes uninhibited development at an age when playing and learning are often synonymous. From ages 7 to 13, children benefit from a single-sex classroom environment,
where girls and boys learn in different and bespoke ways. The moment classes finish, everyone is together – at break and lunch as well as for sports, music, clubs and activities. This really is the best of both worlds for our children.
“ The children pretty much mix in every aspect except for actual academic lessons. Could it be we have stumbled across the perfect school model?”
Academically ambitious, pastorally focused
With more grammar school places than any other school in the local area, we challenge children to think and work ambitiously. Children flourish in our innovative learning environment, following our creative curriculum from age 2, before progressing to the Pre-Senior Baccalaureate programme at age 7. Teachers really invest in the children
and know them well, with lessons carefully planned to cater to all abilities. We approach the welfare of our pupils in a positive way, and all our staff reinforce the Somerhill philosophy and ethos. Our children feel happy and secure, and look forward to coming to school each day.
“ Broad and well-designed curriculum… regularly reviewed to ensure it continues to meet the needs of all the pupils.”
“P ositive mental health is given high priority’ and ‘the welfare of pupils is given prime importance.” Independent Schools Inspectorate — February 2024
Outdoor learning at its best
Making the most of our extensive grounds, indoor and outdoor learning blend naturally at Somerhill. From collecting and counting logs in the woods for maths, to fun French day activities on the formal lawns, children are immersed in our beautiful surroundings every day. For those in Nursery and Kindergarten, we offer a bespoke outdoor learning provision, Saplings. Based on the principles of Forest
School, children experience and explore our dedicated outdoor woodland area, fostering a sense of curiosity and imagination. Inspired by the changing seasons, activities are designed to take advantage of our beautiful and natural environment. Every day is an adventure; not even the wettest and muddiest conditions will keep Somerhill pupils from exploring!
“ When they come inside and sit at their desks, I want to see their muddy knees from playing in the parkland.”
Somerhill’s setting creates endless opportunities… Our classroom learning is further enhanced by our extensive range of extra-curricular activities and after-school clubs. With over 100 weekly activities, this really is a get stuck into everything kind of place.

Our vision and values
At Somerhill, we help each pupil achieve their best possible all-round development. Children discover themselves and develop their talents here, with the wholehearted support of our caring community. Taking a holistic approach to education, we nurture academic, personal, spiritual, social and moral growth, enabling our pupils to
become confident, curious and resilient individuals as they go out into the world. We encourage our pupils to work hard and take pride in their achievements, to think independently, to face up to challenges, to accept responsibility, to develop a broad range of skills and interests, and to show concern for others and the environment.
Somerhill 2030 strategic vision
Our Somerhill 2030 strategic vision is an ambitious plan to shape the next phase of our school direction. Having passed our 30th anniversary at the Somerhill site in 2020, we are now looking to the future. Conscious of being sensitive and respectful of the past, we are equally visionary in providing an exceptional education in this unique setting, where the best of co-education and single-sex schooling meet in perfect harmony. Our vision of growing amazing people has, at its heart, the fundamental priority of delivering an outstanding educational experience for our pupils. Devised with the purpose of keeping abreast of the very best educational practices and providing cutting-edge facilities, this makes Somerhill the prep school of choice. We stand today as a thriving school of over 500 pupils from 2-13 years, yet we are not complacent
about our future. To be dynamic and provide the modern education Somerhill children need to succeed in the future, we ensure that they are as confident in the digital domain as in the natural world. We grow independent thinkers in whom we foster resilience, to become socially responsible people with a strong moral compass; individuals that are driven by strong values and a deep care for each other. We give them the confidence and skills to manage in an ever-changing world. Somerhill will continue to be, above all, a warm, happy and safe place for children to explore and learn. Our pupils pastoral care and well-being are our priorities along with a broad and balanced education. This approach builds robust foundations, ensuring they leave Somerhill with a growth mindset and a strong attitude to learning, ready to embrace future challenges as amazing people.

At the same time, we recognise that every child’s journey is different. Around 40 pupils currently receive tailored learning support, ensuring that every Somerhill pupil is challenged, nurtured and encouraged to achieve their personal best.
At Somerhill, we are proud of our ambitious and high-achieving pupils, who consistently secure places at top senior schools. Each year, we send more pupils to grammar school than any other local school, with destinations including Tonbridge Grammar School, The Judd School, The Skinners’ School and many others. Our broad and balanced curriculum
The Somerhill curriculum is about developing a curious, confident attitude through skills- based learning. Our diverse curriculum is a programme of study that prepares pupils for the challenges of life, personally, socially, culturally, and spiritually. All pupils are encouraged, recognised, and celebrated for their achievements.
We are continually seeking ways to broaden our pupils’ education with relevant and engaging activities that develop a range of skills to prepare them for the future. Our younger children learn through our creative curriculum from Nursery to Year 2, and from Year 3 to 8 we follow the Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB).
GRAPHICS for results, scholarships and destinations?
Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB): A 21st century education
We are proud to be a flagship school for the PSB programme. The PSB is about challenging perceptions of school and developing a love of learning. This is best achieved by children developing a clear understanding of their skills and their areas for development. The PSB assessment framework focuses on six key areas: leadership, collaboration, independence, thinking and learning, reviewing and improving, and communication. By focusing on these core skills, children are best equipped
to deal with the challenges and opportunities of senior school life and beyond. The PSB, with its focus on building a full range of skills, reflects our vision for how children are educated at Somerhill. ‘Non-cognitive skills and attributes such as teamwork, emotional maturity and empathy are as important as proficiency in English and mathematics in ensuring young people’s employment prospects.’ – The Pearson Report
Pastoral care at Somerhill
We approach the welfare of our pupils in a positive way, and all our staff reinforce the Somerhill philosophy and ethos. Somerhill children are happy, secure and look forward to coming to school each day. Our children feel able to talk freely and openly to any staff member if they have any worries or problems of any kind. Staff respond appropriately to children, offering advice, support, guidance and reassurance.
Somerhill shapes a pastoral support programme for individual children, where necessary, to manage their particular needs. We also have a trained school counsellor available to work with pupils during the school day. All staff, from our Headteacher and senior leaders to class teachers, SENCOs, and non-teaching staff, are invested in the outstanding pastoral care at Somerhill.
All children are asked to participate in a taster day before an offer of a place is made. If your child is in Reception to Year 8, they will be teamed up with a ‘buddy’ who has similar interests and will attend lessons and activities during a typical school day. Taster days allow your child to understand and engage with school life and encourage a smooth transition when moving schools.
Our three most common entry points at Somerhill are Nursery, Reception and Year 3. Children can join us anytime during the school year, subject to availability. Our youngest pupils can join us for our Nursery provision when they are two years old. Children may also join in September after their third birthday when they can join our Kindergarten for the school year before Reception. Children are also welcome to join Somerhill directly at Reception. Once you decide you would like your child to join Somerhill, you must complete our registration form and pay a £180 (incl VAT) fee per child. This is a non-refundable registration fee.
Supplementary information
The taster day experience is as much for your child as it is for us here at Somerhill; it is a chance to assess whether we are a suitable fit for your child and can offer a happy school life and all the support they need. Following a successful taster day, a place offer will be made. Our offer will include information on fees, term dates, and our terms and conditions. If your child is currently attending a school that is a member of IAPS, we will need to contact them (with your permission) to check they are aware and that everything is in order. Extra-curricular clubs and activities
‘This really is a get stuck into everything kind of place’
Our extensive range of extra-curricular activities and after-school clubs further enhance our classroom learning. Somerhill’s unique setting allows for endless opportunities, and every inch of our diverse and expansive site is exploited during break times, lunch times, during lessons and after-school clubs.
Despite its size, our extra-curricular activities are not limited to the Somerhill estate. We have multiple trips and off-site adventures taking place every week.

Pastoral care and safeguarding at Somerhill
Outstanding pastoral care
We approach the welfare of our pupils in a positive way, and all our staff reinforce the Somerhill philosophy and ethos. Somerhill children are happy, secure and look forward to coming to school each day.
Our children feel able to talk freely and openly to any staff member if they have any worries or problems of any kind. Staff respond appropriately to children, offering advice, support, guidance and reassurance. Somerhill shapes a pastoral support programme for individual children, where necessary, to manage their particular needs. We also have a trained school counsellor available to work with pupils during the school day.
All staff, from our Senior Leadership Team to class teachers, SENCOs, and non-teaching staff, are invested in the outstanding pastoral care at Somerhill.
Well-being and happiness
At Somerhill, we want our pupils to develop academically, but most of all we give them space to be themselves, enjoy their childhood and fulfil their individual potential. Our aim is to grow amazing people, and we support our pupils in being happy, confident and able to make a positive contribution to our school and the wider world.
With our outstanding grounds and sports facilities, there are plenty of opportunities for children at Somerhill to develop their physical health, but mental health and self-esteem are just as important and looking out for one another is promoted in school. We have a buddy system where older pupils guide and advise younger ones, and all our pupils have a strong bond with their class and form teachers. Our school counsellor also works weekly with pupils who have particular pastoral care needs. All this means there is always someone to talk to.
Our pastoral care is further supported by the addition of our Mindfulness Gazebo in 2024. This is a safe space within the Somerhill estate where pupils and staff can read, relax and take time out to be mindful and thoughtful throughout the day.
Safeguarding at Somerhill
Safeguarding is taken very seriously at Somerhill to ensure all pupils and staff are as safe as possible in and out of school.
We are a community, and all those directly connected (staff, governors, volunteers, parents, families and pupils) have an essential role to play in making it safe and secure. Our broad and balanced curriculum
Our broad and balanced curriculum
Our diverse curriculum is designed to develop a curious, confident attitude through skills-based learning and prepares pupil for the challenges of life, personally, socially, culturally, and spiritually.
All pupils are encouraged, recognised, and celebrated for their achievements. We are continually seeking ways to broaden our pupils’ education with relevant and engaging activities that develop a range of skills to prepare them for the future.
Our younger children learn through our creative curriculum from Nursery to Year 2, and from Year 3 to 8 we follow the Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB).
Early years’ curriculum
We foster a love of learning in our pupils at the earliest possible stage. The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum focuses on three prime areas of learning: communication and language, physical development, and personal, social and emotional development. These are fundamental to supporting children's development. In addition, the curriculum includes four specific areas: literacy, mathematics, understanding the world, and expressive arts and design, all of which build on the foundation set by the prime areas. Learning is a wonderful mixture of teacher and child-led activities and focuses on holistic development, with well-being at the heart of everything we do.
Pre-prep creative curriculum
Reading, writing, and maths are the core focus in Reception, Year 1, and Year 2.
We launch an exciting new topic each term through our creative curriculum approach, seamlessly linking humanities, science, and art to create a dynamic and engaging learning experience. These creative projects not only deepen children’s understanding but also spark their curiosity and passion for learning.
By exploring topics holistically, pupils gain a richer understanding of the world, with every subject reinforcing and enhancing the others. This approach makes learning both relevant and engaging, helping children retain knowledge while developing a wide range of skills. The results speak for themselves, with pupils showing heightened engagement and a more integrated understanding of their subjects.
This approach also nurtures essential life skills such as teamwork, research, critical thinking, and problem-solving, empowering children to grow both academically and personally. All of this prepares our children for success beyond the classroom.
Academic curriculum in prep
Timetabled lessons from Year 3 include art, digital literacy, engineering, English, French, games, geography, history, Latin, mathematics, music, PE/swimming, personal social and health education (PSHE), philosophy, religion and ethics, and science. All subjects are taught in single-sex classes.
Some of the wider learning areas we focus on are:
Our pupils make good use of information and communication technology to gain practical skills for the future and support their learning in all areas of the curriculum. All Key Stage 2 and 3 pupils have a digital literacy lesson once a week, and children from Year 5 build webpages to showcase their online portfolio. Staying safe in the digital world is a key aspect of teaching in all year groups.
We have placed STEM (science, technology, engineering and maths) at the heart of our curriculum at Somerhill. These are skills we feel strongly about as we prepare children for an ever-changing world. Our engineering programme evolved from our innovative design technology (IDT) curriculum, which grew pupils’ knowledge of applying software to products and covered topics such as robotics and electronics. We are always thinking ahead and looking to use new technologies such as augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality. Some classes have already created their own AR displays.
Our curriculum focuses on three core themes: health and well-being, relationships and living in the wider world. Within these themes, we cover topics such as emotions, family and friends, health, economic awareness and enterprise. We encourage pupils to contribute to discussions and express their thoughts.
Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB): A 21st century education
We are proud to be a flagship school for the PSB programme. The PSB is about challenging perceptions of school and developing a love of learning. This is best achieved by children developing a clear understanding of their skills and their areas for development.
The PSB assessment framework focuses on six key areas: leadership, collaboration, independence, thinking and learning, reviewing and improving, and communication. By focusing on these core skills, children are best equipped to deal with the challenges and opportunities of senior school life and beyond.
The PSB, with its focus on building a full range of skills, reflects our vision for how children are educated at Somerhill.
‘Non-cognitive skills and attributes such as teamwork, emotional maturity and empathy are as important as proficiency in English and mathematics in ensuring young people’s employment prospects.’ - The Pearson Report
Please visit the PSB website for more information on the Pre-Senior Baccalaureate programme.
Parents as partners
We believe that a strong home-school partnership is key to enhancing and supporting children's learning. Our open-door approach fosters strong relationships with parents, ensuring open communication and mutual trust. The more we connect and collaborate, the better we can support your child's development, creating a shared commitment to their education and well-being.

pageCache.text:
Our history and heritage
Once a family home, now a family school
Somerhill is unique in that it is the coming together of three individual schools on one beautiful and historic site.
Yardley Court was a boy's school, founded in 1898 in Tonbridge, which moved to Somerhill in 1990 to accommodate its expansion and meet growing demand.
Derwent Lodge, a school for girls established in the 1930s in Tunbridge Wells, also relocated to Somerhill in 1993 as their former home could no longer support the school’s growth. Shortly after, Somerhill Pre-Prep was founded in 1995 to complete our educational offerings.
These three schools operated independently as The Schools at Somerhill until 2018, when we recognised the opportunity to unify them into the vibrant community we have today with shared facilities, a common vision, and a collective purpose.
Today, we are one thriving school. We are proud of our heritage and carry it with us as we move forward as Somerhill.
In 2011, our mansion celebrated its 400th year. In its lifetime, it’s been through periods of growth, decline and restoration, and seen great families come and go. From the 1600s to the present day, here is a look back at the history of Somerhill, and how it became the home of our happy, modern school.
The land of Somerhill was part of the Manor of South Frith, an expansive estate owned by the Crown. The manor was used for hunting and timber before reverting fully to the Crown during the Tudor period.
Queen Elizabeth I granted the land to Frances Walsingham, daughter of Sir Francis Walsingham, her Secretary of State. This gift reflected the close ties between the monarch and her trusted advisors.
Sir Philip Sidney, Frances Walsingham’s first husband and a renowned poet, diplomat, and soldier, died from wounds sustained at the Battle of Zutphen. Frances inherited a portion of his wealth and social influence.
Frances’ second husband, Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex, was executed for treason after leading a failed rebellion against Elizabeth I. Frances was left poverty stricken – all Devereux’s money had gone to pay his debts. It was probably around this time that Elizabeth granted the Somerhill land to Frances. Frances later married Richard Burke, 4th Earl of Clanricarde, securing her position in Irish nobility.
Richard and Frances chose a site to build their new house with commanding vistas and natural beauty. Tunbridge Wells did not then exist (the Chalybeate Spring was first seen by Lord North in 1606). Tonbridge was a huge parish, in fact the largest in Kent, stretching from the foot of the Greensand (Sevenoaks) Ridge to the Sussex border. Construction of Somerhill House began under King James I. A first draft of a plan in Sir John Soane’s Museum suggests John Thorpe was the architect. Thorpe designed houses for a number of families in England around that time.
Although Somerhill is clearly Jacobean in style – like the huge house of the Sackvilles at nearby Knole, Sevenoaks – the design follows architectural rules fashionably derived from Andrea di Pietro, alias Palladio, in his famous classical renaissance villa at Vicenza, near Venice. Until this time, large houses had been built with the central hall going across the building, but Somerhill has the hall running the length of the house. This makes the house one of the most innovative in the country for its time. One of the most remarkable survivors at Somerhill is the complete set of original ornamented lead rainwater heads and rain pipes. The rainwater heads are at their most elaborate on the front of the mansion, some dating from 1611 or 1613. Many bear the initials of Robert and Frances Clanricarde, RCF.
Ulick, the son of Frances and Richard Burke, 4th Earl of Clanricarde, fought for the Royalist cause. After the royalist defeat at the Battle of Naseby in 1645, Somerhill was sequestered by parliament and Ulick forced into exile. Bradshaw died in 1659, and the house passed to his son. Bradshaw was given a huge funeral at St Peter’s church in Westminster, but a year later his body was dug up and hanged on the gallows at Tyburn.
Parliament granted the house to Robert Devereux, 3rd Earl of Essex, a prominent Parliamentarian. After his death, it was transferred to John Bradshaw, President of the High Court of Justice for Charles I’s trial.
John Bradshaw, a key figure in the execution of Charles I in 1649 (John Bradshaw is the first signature on the famous death warrant), died, leaving the house to his son. The estate remained under Parliamentary control until the monarchy was restored.
Following Charles II's restoration, the estate was returned to Ulick’s daughter, Margaret Burke, Lady Muskerry. This act was part of a broader effort to restore Royalist families' properties.
Around this time the new Tunbridge Wells became fashionable with London nobility. Before adequate lodgings were developed around the Pantiles, Lady Muskerry – like certain other nearby big houses – hosted many gentry visiting the Wells to socialise and to take the waters.
In 1664 the Queen visited Tunbridge Wells; the Queen’s ladies stayed at Somerhill and ‘went every day to court or the court came to them’. However, the family sold the estate to cover gambling debts, a common downfall among aristocratic families of the period.
The estate was purchased by Thomas Deakins, a wealthy local merchant, who established a charitable fund for the poor in Tonbridge, demonstrating the emerging philanthropy of the rising merchant class. The Lowy of Tunbridge states: ‘Thomas Deakins, gent. of Tunbridge, in 1707, gave to this parish 50l. to put out ten poor boys apprentices; and 50l. more to the poor, which was laid out in building two almshouses.’
In 1712, the estate came into the possession of the Woodgate family. John Woodgate (1664-1727) bought the house now known as Somerhill. Their association with the area is remembered in Woodgate Way, and William Woodgate’s portrait still hangs in the Long Library at Somerhill. By this stage the house was somewhat neglected. Horace Walpole, who was touring Kent, remarked: ‘The house is little better than a farm, but has been an excellent one and is entire, though out of repair.’
The Woodgates were an important Tonbridge family in the 18th and 19th centuries. John Woodgate had 13 children, one of whom, Henry, inherited both Somerhill and Stonewall in 1728 and played a full part in public life; he promoted the Medway navigation scheme and left money for an organ in the parish church. Since Henry did not have children, he made his nephew William (1743-1809) his heir. William was the son of Henry’s brother Francis (1706-90) who had become a curate at Seal, married a local lady and was then given the living of Mountfield in Sussex by the Duke of Dorset.
William married Frances Hooker, built up a considerable fortune and bought the new house (built by his brother-in-law Thomas Hooker) attached to Tonbridge Castle in 1793 for his son, William Francis (1770-1828). William Woodgate’s participation in town life included sending his sons to Tonbridge School, serving as a magistrate, financing the new Town Hall in 1798 (just north of the Big Bridge) and owning about a dozen properties in the town.
After William died, William Francis (‘The Major’) moved to Somerhill and made improvements to it. He had at least 10 children, and one of his daughters married Dr Thomas Knox, the headmaster of Tonbridge School. During the threat of a Napoleonic invasion, William Francis commanded a troop of about 55 cavalry volunteers, as part of the West Kent Yeomanry, who were raised from among local inhabitants in 1794.
William Francis’s father had been one of three founders of the Tonbridge Bank in 1792 but in 1816 the Bank failed, bringing ruin to its backers. In addition to this, the Woodgates were hit hard by the agricultural depression at the end of the Napoleonic Wars and sold Somerhill the same year. The victorious Duke of Wellington declined to buy Somerhill, dissatisfied by its fox hunting! William Francis was forced to sell Somerhill. Although the Woodgates no longer lived in Somerhill after that date, another member of the family, Francis (1781-1843), returned to live in Tonbridge in 1823 when he bought Ferox Hall.
James Alexander (1769-1848) became the new owner of the Somerhill estate. He obtained JMW Turner’s painting, completed in 1811, of the grounds and building before it was sold to the National Gallery of Scotland, its current home. It’s thought that Turner painted the scene for the Woodgate family. His viewpoint was the lakeside looking up through the trees towards the house on the ridge. The honey-coloured stonework is bathed in warm, soft evening light. The painting is probably the most exquisite example of Turner’s transformation of the tradition of the topographical house portrait.
James Alexander acquired one of the stone coffins that were found at Tonbridge Priory when the ruins were demolished to make way for the railway. This is still on the Somerhill site, currently in the Rose Garden.
In 1849, Somerhill estate, which once covered 6,500 acres (2,600 ha), was bought by Sir Isaac Lyon Goldsmid, 1st Baronet, a rich City banker. He passed the house to his second son, Frederick, in 1859 and then it went to Frederick’s elder son, Sir Julian, in 1866. Julian’s attempt at providing a male heir – he had eight daughters – eventually resulted in a virtual doubling of the house’s living accommodation. Building work began in 1879 (according to dated rainwater heads) and was completed as the new stable court, with clock tower, in Queen Victoria’s Diamond Jubilee year, 1897. The old, Jacobean, stable court became servants’ rooms and domestic offices. The terraces and lawns were added at this stage and the estate took on much of its present appearance. Today, the house is the second largest in Kent, after Knole, covering about two and a half acres (one hectare) and with about 270 rooms.
On the death of Sir Julian, and in accordance with Sir Isaac’s will (to pass the house through male heirs), the house went to a grandson of his aunt Rachel, who was married to Count Solomon D’Avigdor. Osmond D’Avigdor Goldsmid was now the new owner.
It is thought the imitative Jacobean barrel ceiling was put up in the (Grand) Salon at this stage. Later it was given a flat Jacobean style and a suite of maids’ rooms and nurseries were inserted above. The room was also extensively re-panelled, with wainscoting and carved frieze also added. The Entrance Hall below was re-panelled, its ornate Italian plaster ceiling renovated. The Jacobean-style chimney piece in the adjoining room was retained (its features being the reverse of those seen on a fine chimney piece at Knole). This chimney piece of polychrome marble probably dates from around 1878, although some visitors to the house have said it was brought over in the 1930s from Italy. The library, running 30 metres (93 feet) – the full length of the south wing and reputedly the second longest room in Kent, after the Gallery at Knole – was also refurbished.
During the summer months of 1912 an army camp is said to have been held (in bell tents) in the grounds and, in the Second World War, Somerhill was known as POW Camp No 40. The army occupied the land from 1940 to 1945.
The Diary of Vinzenz Fetzer, a prisoner-of-war in Tonbridge during the Second World War, who spent three years at POW Camp No 40, gives a fascinating insight into the Somerhill site during this time.
In 1948, homeless people occupied parts of the area, and the Army Colonel in charge ‘locked the squatters in’, apparently assisted by old barbed wire.
In 1949, the local council had discussions regarding the land, and it’s said there were at least 40 huts of varying sizes. Sir Osmond died in 1940 and was succeeded by his elder son, Sir Henry.
During the Goldsmid family’s residence at Somerhill in the 20th century, there was some lavish entertaining. Sir Henry’s wife, Rosemary D’Avigdor Goldsmid, once likened the place to a hotel, except the guests never paid! Occasionally guests included royalty, and stories abound about the time spent at the house by David Niven, Enoch Powell, Sir Hugh Casson, Sir John Betjeman and others. Sir Hugh, a good family friend, designed the small changing pavilion by the swimming pool.
In the closing years of the family’s residence, a much-loved daughter, Sarah, drowned off the south coast. The artist Marc Chagall, who was known to the family, was commissioned to design stunning new memorial windows in nearby Tudeley church. There is also a commemorative stone in the gardens beyond Yardley Court’s war memorial lychgate.
On Sir Henry’s death in 1976, Somerhill passed to his sole surviving daughter, Chloe – now Chloe Teacher – who lives at Hadlow Place Farm with her family. Lady D’Avigdor Goldsmid died in 1997. However, financial challenges and changing priorities led to its eventual sale.
In 1980, after years of neglect, Somerhill House was sold with the gardens and parkland. The property then changed hands three times in eight years, during which time more neglect, decay and storm damage took its toll. The first new owner, in an act of ignorance bordering on vandalism, removed the carved wooden hall screen and over-stained large areas of panelling in the entrance hall and upstairs salon.
What we see today is little short of a miracle. From 1989-91, the house was extensively repaired and restored. Some 12 miles of cables were used in the re-wiring! The main contractors were the family firm Durtnells of Brasted, near Sevenoaks – the oldest building firm in Britain. In 1991, as work drew to a close, the firm celebrated its 400th anniversary with a big party at Somerhill – one of a number of local houses which the firm is very likely to have helped build!
Any restoration and development for the school’s use is handled sensitively, in consultation with conservation experts, but the building has proved remarkably well suited to its modern

Our unique structure
One way of living but two ways of learning
At Somerhill, we have one way of living but two ways of learning. Between the ages of 2 and 7 years, girls and boys are together in the classroom. This environment promotes uninhibited development at an age when playing and learning are often synonymous. From 7 to 13 years, children benefit from a single-sex classroom environment, where girls and boys learn in different and bespoke ways.
The moment classes finish, everyone is together - at break and lunch as well as for sports, music, clubs and activities.
This really is the best of both worlds for our children.
Coming together, from three schools into one
Yardley Court was a boy's school founded in 1898 in Tonbridge and came to the Somerhill site in 1990 in order to expand. Derwent Lodge, a school for girls, was established in the 1930s and followed in 1993, moving from their Tunbridge Wells town centre home, which they had outgrown. Somerhill Pre-Prep, a co-educational school for ages 2-7, was established in 1995 at Somerhill.
These three schools were separate, as ‘The Schools at Somerhill’, until 2018, when we saw the potential for integrating and building one special school community with shared facilities, vision and purpose.
We stand today as a thriving school of over 500 pupils from the age of 2-13, yet we are not complacent about our future. We set out to be sensitive and respectful of the past, whilst being equally visionary in how we can continue to provide an outstanding education for our young people in this unique setting.
“The perfect educational model…with stonking facilities…the green spaces will make you swoon.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Discover our innovative pre-prep — Somerhill: A leading independent day prep school for boys and girls aged 2-13
pageCache.text:
Pre-prep at Somerhill
The next stage of our Somerhill learning journey
From pre-school, the next exciting step at age 4 is joining Somerhill pre-prep. In Reception, children continue to follow the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum, before transitioning to the national curriculum in Year 1 and 2. This change introduces more structured learning while preserving the creativity and exploration that underpin early education.
As part of our nurturing environment, children move up alongside their friends while also welcoming new classmates who join directly in Reception. We ensure a smooth and confident transition by providing numerous opportunities for children to visit their new classrooms, meet their new teachers, and become familiar with the exciting changes ahead. We focus on making each child feel comfortable and excited as they take the next step in their educational journey.
Pre-prep at Somerhill offers a warm, supportive environment where children develop a love of learning that will last a lifetime. We foster curiosity, confidence, and resilience in our young learners. Our nurturing co-educational environment, tailored for children aged 4 to 7, strongly emphasises children’s well-being, as we believe that learning comes naturally when children are happy and engaged.
Our balanced and dynamic curriculum
Our curriculum is designed to nurture curious, confident, and creative problem-solvers from an early age. With a perfect balance of core subjects and a creative curriculum, we develop excellent academic foundations while encouraging critical thinking, resilience, and creativity. Through project-based learning that connects subjects like geography, history, and art, children explore concepts actively, developing essential life skills such as teamwork and problem-solving.
We make learning meaningful and engaging, whether through hands-on activities in math and English, inspiring a love of reading and writing, or supporting personal growth with the help of our Pre-Prep Pals. Our commitment to a safe, supportive environment ensures every child feels valued and empowered, developing the confidence to tackle challenges positively. With a strong home-school partnership, we work together to ensure each child succeeds and thrives as a lifelong learner.
We have high expectations of our children, but with their well-being in mind, ensuring they feel proud of their progress and accomplishments every step of the way. By nurturing their confidence and resilience, we empower them to take on new challenges with a sense of pride and joy in their learning.
Every class in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2, has a teacher and a teaching assistant to support their academic learning and well-being. We are lucky to have specialist subject teachers who work with all the children, teaching PE, games, swimming, French, music, and woodlands.
‘High-quality education in a happy environment. Teaching enables pupils of all abilities to make progress. It promotes exploration and independent learning and gives pupils confidence in their abilities.’
Independent Schools Inspectorate - February 2024
Staying active in pre-prep
At Somerhill, we believe in the power of outdoor learning and make the most of our beautiful 150-acre estate. Whether it's taking maths, art, creative writing, or science outside, we embrace the natural environment to enhance every subject. Come rain or shine, our confident learners eagerly explore the courtyard, play areas, and lush green spaces across the school. PE, games, woodland adventures, and swimming sessions are woven into the pre-prep timetable from Reception onwards, ensuring children stay active, engaged and connected to nature.
Our outdoor experiences play a key role in fostering a love of learning while supporting physical and emotional development. In preparation for sports in the prep school, Year 2 children begin to have a small amount of match experience with fixtures organised with other schools in the area.
Capturing creativity
Music, drama, and art play a central role in our pre-prep curriculum. With a purpose-built music suite and specialist teachers, children explore singing and early musicianship each week. From Year 2, we encourage pupils to take individual instrumental lessons, celebrating their progress at special teatime concerts throughout the year.
Our array of Christmas performances, drama productions, and the much-anticipated pre-prep show at the end of the year provide wonderful opportunities for children to shine in front of their families.
Art exhibitions showcase the skills and creativity the children develop in class, while many also participate in dance classes offered through our outside partner clubs. These enriching experiences foster creativity and build confidence and emotional resilience, helping our youngest learners grow in self-assurance and express themselves with pride.
Moving up to Somerhill prep
At the end of Year 2, our pre-prep pupils join our Somerhill prep-school. Our teachers have many years of experience helping children (and parents) move up happily from pre-prep to prep and will support them in continuing the Somerhill journey.
We ensure children feel ready and confident in moving to prep, and each summer, we hold several ‘moving-up’ activities, including induction sessions, allowing children to get to know their new classmates and teachers.

Pre-school at Somerhill
The journey begins at our Somerhill pre-school
Pre-school at Somerhill is where children begin their learning journey from age 2. We recognise that every child is unique and develops at their own pace, and both our Nursery and Kindergarten classes provide a nurturing and stimulating environment for our youngest learners. Our caring staff work closely with parents to support their child's well-being, fostering both emotional and academic growth in a safe, secure, and inspiring environment.
Our beautiful grounds provide the perfect setting for both indoor and outdoor learning experiences, with teaching teams collaborating to support each child's individual progress. We are also fortunate to offer specialist teaching in music and PE including balance bike and BEAM (balance, education, and movement), all supported by classroom teachers.
Our classroom learning is enhanced by Saplings, an outdoor programme based on Forest School principles. At Saplings, children explore nature and develop a love for the outdoors, guided by our Forest School-trained staff, who are also qualified teachers. During the pre-school years, you can choose a hybrid model of indoor and outdoor sessions; and this balance of indoor and outdoor learning creates a well-rounded and enriching educational experience.
At Somerhill, we promote a strong emphasis on creativity, independence, and resilience. We are proud to have very happy children here, who thrive in a supportive, engaging, and caring environment; their enthusiasm for learning is at the heart of everything we do.
Making the most of our beautiful surroundings
We use all areas of our wonderful Somerhill estate for activities such as bug hunting, looking for animal homes, spotting signs of seasonal change, and other activities based around maths, literacy, physical development, and all the other things we are learning about in our Somerhill Pre-School.
Pre-school sessions
We try to be as flexible as we can about the number of sessions that you feel your child is ready to attend. There is no requirement or expectation for Kindergarten children to be full time the term before they enter Reception.
However, we do believe that continuity of interaction is important, so we ask that you commit to a minimum of three sessions a week. This can be a combination of three mornings, a day and a half, or two mornings and an afternoon.
Moving to pre-prep
Somerhill pre-school offers a seamless transition into Reception at our Somerhill pre-prep. This continuity helps our children settle quickly and confidently whilst being supported every step of the way.
